pr.body:
Depends on #531.

### The problem

An arrow function without braces ends at the end of its line, but only when
the first token of the next line reaches the rule that ends a statement, and
that token is counted as part of the function. Keywords, modifiers and
brackets are read before that rule, and a line that goes on with the
expression ends it all the same:

```js
function m(key, cursor) {
  switch (true) {
    case key.left:
      return () => cursor.prevWord()
    case key.right:
      return () => cursor.nextWord()
  }
}
const pick = (a, b) => a && b
  ? a
  : b || 0
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       2      2      6      0       2 (anonymous)@4-5@a.js
       2      1      6      0       2 (anonymous)@6-7@a.js
       6      2     31      2       8 m@1-8@a.js
       2      3     10      2       2 pick@9-10@a.js
```

The two arrow functions in `m` end one line late, and the first one takes the
`case` of the next line: `m` has a cyclomatic complexity of 2 instead of 3.
`pick` ends at line 10 and loses the `||` of line 11. A modifier does not end
the function either:

```js
class A {
  handler = () => 1
  async load() {
    return 1
  }
}
function after() { return 1 }
```

```
$ lizard b.js          # master, 01afe9c
       6      1     21      0       6 handler@2-7@b.js
```

`handler` takes the rest of the class and the function after it, so `load`
and `after` are not reported. Also, `const inc = x => x + 1` followed by a line
without a semicolon has NLOC 2 and one token more than with it.

### What changes

`lizard_languages/javascript_functions.py` and
`lizard_languages/typescript_states.py`. The first token of a new line now
ends an arrow function without braces in every state, unless the line starts
with an operator such as `?`, `&&`, `+` or `.`, or the line before ends with
one; the end line, the NLOC, the token and the conditions of that first token
go to the function around it. With the fix:

```
       1      1      5      0       1 (anonymous)@4-4@a.js
       1      1      5      0       1 (anonymous)@6-6@a.js
       8      3     33      2       8 m@1-8@a.js
       3      4     15      2       3 pick@9-11@a.js

       1      1      4      0       1 handler@2-2@b.js
       3      1      6      0       3 load@3-5@b.js
       1      1      6      0       1 after@7-7@b.js
```

### How it is tested

`Test_ES6_arrow_function_without_braces_on_many_lines` in
`test/test_languages/testES6.py`: 5 tests, all failing without the change. The
full suite passes on the branch: `python -m pytest test` gives 1672 passed,
7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

A `;` or a `,` still ends the function as before. #525 makes an arrow function
without braces end at the enclosing `,`: this branch keeps that rule, and a
merge of the two passes the full suite, the tests of #525 included.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.
